reuse.title: Reuse only when safe and clean
reuse.text: If the container can be cleaned safely and its prior contents are known, consider a non-food storage use.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check local container guidance
recycleOrDispose.text: Do not assume an oil container is accepted with ordinary plastic recycling. Follow local instructions for its material and prior contents.

reuse.title: Reuse as a container
reuse.text: If clean and in good condition, consider a non-food storage or gardening use.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check local plastic rules
recycleOrDispose.text: Acceptance can depend on the plastic type and local collection rules. Check local guidance before placing it in recycling.

reuse.title: Keep, repair, or pass it on
reuse.text: If it works, consider continued use or repair before disposal.

recycleOrDispose.title: Use electronics disposal guidance
recycleOrDispose.text: Check local instructions for electronic equipment; do not assume it belongs in ordinary household recycling.

reuse.title: Repair or continue using
reuse.text: If it works safely, continued use or repair may extend its life.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check specialist disposal guidance
recycleOrDispose.text: Follow local guidance for appliances and any refrigerant or electrical handling requirements. Do not dismantle it unless qualified.

reuse.title: Repair or repurpose
reuse.text: Consider mending, repurposing, or using it as a cleaning cloth if appropriate.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check textile collection options
recycleOrDispose.text: Textile recycling and collection options vary by location. Check local guidance for worn or damaged clothing.

reuse.title: Check whether it can be used or composted
reuse.text: If safe and suitable, consider using the food; otherwise check whether a local composting or food-waste program accepts it.

recycleOrDispose.title: Keep food scraps with wet waste
recycleOrDispose.text: Separate food scraps from dry recyclables. Use a suitable home or community composting option if available, or give them to your local wet-waste collection. Check local rules before adding meat, dairy, or cooked food to a home compost pile.

reuse.title: Identify its contents first
reuse.text: Reuse only when you know what it held and can clean it safely. Do not use a former chemical container for food or drinking water.

recycleOrDispose.title: Choose a more specific container
recycleOrDispose.text: The material and any remaining contents change the disposal route. Choose a specific item or add its material and check local collection rules.

reuse.title: Reuse an intact jar or bottle
reuse.text: If it is clean and undamaged, use it again for suitable storage or crafts.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check glass collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Empty the container and check whether your local collector accepts this type of glass. Keep broken glass safely wrapped and follow local instructions.

reuse.title: Repurpose a safe can
reuse.text: An empty, clean can without sharp edges may work as a holder or planter.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check metal packaging collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Empty the can and ask your local collector whether it accepts metal food or drink cans. A can that held paint or chemicals needs separate guidance.

reuse.title: Use the box again
reuse.text: A dry, sturdy box can be reused for packing, storage, or moving.

recycleOrDispose.title: Keep cardboard dry
recycleOrDispose.text: Flatten clean, dry boxes if your local collector accepts cardboard. Wet or food-soiled cardboard may need another route.

reuse.title: Reuse while sturdy
reuse.text: Use a clean, intact bag for carrying or storing dry items.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check paper collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Clean, dry paper bags may be accepted with paper. Check local rules for coated or food-soiled bags.

reuse.title: Reuse only when appropriate
reuse.text: A clean, undamaged container can be repurposed. Do not assume single-use packaging is safe for heating or long-term food storage.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check the container type
recycleOrDispose.text: Empty and clean it where practical, then check whether local collection accepts this type of plastic container.

reuse.title: Use intact bags again
reuse.text: An intact, clean bag can be reused for carrying or lining a bin.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check film-specific collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Flexible films and wrappers may be handled differently from rigid plastic bottles. Check local acceptance before mixing them with other recyclables.

reuse.title: Repair or pass on a working phone
reuse.text: If it is safe and usable, consider repair or reuse. Back up and erase personal data before passing it on.

recycleOrDispose.title: Find an e-waste collection route
recycleOrDispose.text: Ask the producer or a local authorised collection or recycling service how to hand over the phone. Do not put it in ordinary dry recycling.

reuse.title: Repair or pass on a working computer
reuse.text: Consider repair or reuse if safe. Back up and erase personal data before giving it away.

recycleOrDispose.title: Use an e-waste route
recycleOrDispose.text: Check producer take-back or an authorised e-waste collection option. Keep batteries and components intact unless a qualified service advises otherwise.

reuse.title: Keep a working mouse in use
reuse.text: If the mouse and its receiver or charging cable still work, consider using it as a spare or passing it on with its accessories.

recycleOrDispose.title: Use an e-waste collection route
recycleOrDispose.text: Ask a producer take-back service or an authorised e-waste collector about the mouse. If it has a removable battery, follow the product instructions and local battery collection guidance; do not put either item in ordinary dry recycling.

reuse.title: Keep a safe, working spare
reuse.text: Reuse a compatible charger or cable only if its insulation and connectors are undamaged.

recycleOrDispose.title: Ask an e-waste collector
recycleOrDispose.text: Check whether a local e-waste service accepts chargers, adapters, and cables. Do not mix them with ordinary metal packaging.

reuse.title: Repair or pass on a working fridge
reuse.text: If it cools reliably and is safe, consider repair or reuse before disposal.

recycleOrDispose.title: Arrange specialist appliance collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Ask the producer or an authorised collector how to handle the appliance and refrigerant. Do not cut pipes or dismantle it yourself.

reuse.title: Repair or pass on a working machine
reuse.text: Consider repair or reuse if it operates safely and does not leak.

recycleOrDispose.title: Use an appliance collection route
recycleOrDispose.text: Check producer take-back or authorised e-waste collection for the complete machine. Confirm pickup arrangements locally.

reuse.title: Repair or reuse if safe
reuse.text: A working appliance may be useful to someone else. Do not reuse one with damaged wiring or unsafe operation.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check appliance e-waste collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Ask a local e-waste service whether it accepts this exact appliance. Remove loose batteries only if the product instructions say this is safe.

reuse.title: Clean or repair the pair
reuse.text: If the soles and uppers are usable, clean or repair the shoes for continued use.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check footwear collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Shoes combine several materials and are not automatically accepted with textile recycling. Ask local collectors about worn footwear.

reuse.title: Repair or reuse the bag
reuse.text: Clean the bag and repair simple damage such as a loose strap or zipper if practical.

recycleOrDispose.title: Identify the bag's materials
recycleOrDispose.text: Fabric, leather, and plastic bags can require different collection routes. Check local options for the main material and condition.

reuse.title: Keep textiles in use
reuse.text: Clean bedsheets and towels can be reused, repaired, or cut into suitable cleaning cloths.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check textile collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Ask local textile collectors whether they accept worn or damaged household linens. Keep unsuitable or contaminated textiles separate.

reuse.title: Share readable books
reuse.text: Pass on books in readable condition to people, libraries, or organisations that confirm they want them.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check paper collection
recycleOrDispose.text: For books that cannot be reused, ask your local collector about covers, bindings, and paper collection requirements.

reuse.title: Repair or pass on sturdy furniture
reuse.text: Clean and repair the piece where practical. Check that it is stable and safe before giving it away.

recycleOrDispose.title: Ask about bulky-item collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Furniture may contain wood, metal, fabric, and foam. Check local bulky-waste or material-specific collection options.

reuse.title: Pass on safe, complete toys
reuse.text: Clean and check for missing parts, sharp edges, and working electronics before reuse.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check the toy's materials
recycleOrDispose.text: A toy may combine plastic, fabric, metal, or electronics. Check local instructions for its components and any batteries.

reuse.title: Compost where suitable
reuse.text: If you have a suitable compost setup, plant scraps may be useful there. Follow the rules of your composting method or collection service.

recycleOrDispose.title: Keep with accepted wet waste
recycleOrDispose.text: Separate peels from dry recyclables and check your local wet-waste or compost collection instructions.

reuse.title: Mulch or compost suitable trimmings
reuse.text: Clean leaves and small plant trimmings may be useful as mulch or compost, if suitable for your setup.

recycleOrDispose.title: Separate leaves and plant trimmings
recycleOrDispose.text: Keep untreated leaves and small plant trimmings separate for composting or local garden-waste collection. Ask your collector about branches; keep painted or treated wood out of compost.

reuse.text: Check whether the item is safe and working before considering reuse or donation. For a broken or unwanted electrical item, use a designated e-waste route and follow local instructions.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check the appropriate collection route

recycleOrDispose.title: Check the appropriate collection route

reuse.title: Use clean sheets again
reuse.text: Use blank sides for notes or crafts when practical.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check paper collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Keep paper clean and dry when possible. Ask your local collector about coated or food-soiled paper.

reuse.title: Reuse sturdy cardboard
reuse.text: Use clean boxes or sheets for storage and packing.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check cardboard collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Flatten dry cardboard if requested locally. Ask about greasy or heavily soiled pieces.

reuse.title: Reuse intact glass
reuse.text: Clean, unbroken containers may be useful again for appropriate storage.

recycleOrDispose.title: Identify the glass item
recycleOrDispose.text: Bottles, window glass, and cookware may have different collection rules. Check local acceptance for the exact item.

reuse.title: Keep usable metal items
reuse.text: Repair or repurpose a safe, usable item where practical.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check metal collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Collection depends on the item, its size, and any coatings or contents. Check local instructions.

reuse.title: Keep sound iron or steel in use
reuse.text: Repair or repurpose a safe, sturdy item if practical.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check ferrous metal collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Ask a local scrap or recycling service whether it accepts this iron or steel item. Paint, coatings, and attached materials may change the route.

reuse.title: Reuse sound aluminium items
reuse.text: Keep a safe, usable item in service or repurpose it where practical.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check aluminium collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Ask a local collector whether it accepts this form of aluminium. Empty containers and check for coatings or attached materials.

recycleOrDispose.title: Identify the specific plastic item
recycleOrDispose.text: Plastic recycling acceptance varies by item, resin, contamination, and local rules. Identify the item and check local instructions.

recycleOrDispose.title: Use electronics disposal guidance
recycleOrDispose.text: Electronic items often need a designated collection route. Check local instructions for the specific item.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check textile collection options
recycleOrDispose.text: Textile collection rules vary. Check local guidance for the specific item and its condition.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check local organic-waste rules
recycleOrDispose.text: Composting and food-waste programs accept different materials. Check the rules for your area.

reuse.title: Reuse safe timber
reuse.text: Clean, sound wood may be used for repair or small projects.

recycleOrDispose.title: Identify treated or painted wood
recycleOrDispose.text: Untreated, painted, and chemically treated wood can need different handling. Check local collection instructions for the exact item.

reuse.title: Repair or repurpose if safe
reuse.text: A reusable rubber item may be repaired or used again depending on its condition.

recycleOrDispose.title: Find an item-specific route
recycleOrDispose.text: Rubber items vary widely. Identify the item, such as footwear or a tyre, before checking local collection options.

reuse.title: Repair or repurpose intact pieces
reuse.text: A sound ceramic item may still be useful for its original purpose or as a planter.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check ceramic disposal
recycleOrDispose.text: Ceramics are not the same as bottle glass. Ask your local collector how to handle broken pottery or crockery, and protect anyone handling sharp pieces.

reuse.title: Repair or reuse leather
reuse.text: A usable leather item may be cleaned, repaired, or passed on if appropriate.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check leather collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Leather is not automatically accepted with fabric or paper. Ask a local collector about the specific item and any synthetic layers or coatings.

reuse.title: Reuse sound copper items
reuse.text: Keep a safe, usable copper item in service or repurpose it where practical.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check copper collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Clean, identifiable copper may have a material-specific scrap route. Ask a local collector what forms and attached components it accepts.

reuse.title: Reuse sound brass items
reuse.text: Keep a safe, usable brass item in service or repurpose it where practical.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check brass collection
recycleOrDispose.text: Identify brass items and ask a local scrap or recycling service whether it accepts this form, including any coatings or attached materials.

recycleOrDispose.title: Separate what you can identify
recycleOrDispose.text: Avoid treating mixed waste as one recyclable material. Identify and separate reusable items, dry recyclables, organic waste, and anything needing special handling, then follow local collection instructions.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check composting conditions
recycleOrDispose.text: Biodegradable does not always mean suitable for home composting. Check the product and local program instructions.

recycleOrDispose.title: Choose a route by material
recycleOrDispose.text: Do not put this item in compost based on its appearance. Identify its material and check the local reuse, recycling, or disposal route.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check the composting label
recycleOrDispose.text: Check what conditions the product requires and whether your home system or local collection accepts it. A compostable label does not guarantee acceptance everywhere.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check special handling guidance
recycleOrDispose.text: Do not assume potentially hazardous items belong in ordinary recycling or household waste. Follow local instructions for the specific material.

recycleOrDispose.title: Check the previous contents
recycleOrDispose.text: Do not assume a container with oil or chemical residue can enter ordinary recycling. Follow local handling instructions for the substance it held.

recycleOrDispose.title: Protect people handling broken pieces
recycleOrDispose.text: Keep sharp or broken pieces contained so nobody is cut. Check local instructions before placing them in any recycling or waste collection.

television.title: Use an e-waste collection route
television.text: Televisions are listed under India's E-Waste (Management) Rules. Ask the producer about take-back or contact a registered producer, refurbisher, or recycler for collection options. Confirm what is available in your city.

sources.title: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 — Schedule I
CPCB E-Waste FAQ

air-conditioner.title: Use an e-waste collection route
air-conditioner.text: Air conditioners, excluding centralised plants, are listed under India's E-Waste (Management) Rules. Ask the producer about take-back or contact a registered producer, refurbisher, or recycler for handling and collection options. Do not dismantle the unit yourself.

sources.title: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 — Schedule I
CPCB E-Waste FAQ

food-scraps.title: Separate food scraps as wet waste
food-scraps.text: Keep food scraps out of dry recycling. Compost suitable scraps at home or use your local wet-waste collection; ask the collector how it handles cooked food and animal products.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — source segregation

fruit-vegetable-peels.title: Put peels in the wet-waste stream
fruit-vegetable-peels.text: Keep fruit and vegetable peels separate from dry recyclables. Compost them if your setup accepts them, or give them to your local wet-waste collection.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — wet waste

garden-trimmings.title: Keep plant trimmings apart from dry recycling
garden-trimmings.text: Compost suitable leaves and small trimmings or ask your local collector about garden-waste collection. Check how it handles large branches.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — wet waste and processing

batteries.title: Use a separate battery collection route
batteries.text: Keep spent batteries out of ordinary dry recycling. Ask the seller, producer, or local authority for a designated take-back or collection point; do not open or burn them.

sources.title: Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022

vehicle-batteries.title: Return a vehicle battery separately
vehicle-batteries.text: Do not mix a vehicle battery with metal scrap or ordinary waste. Ask the seller, producer, or local authority for a battery take-back or designated collection point; request specialist help if it is leaking.

sources.title: Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022

power-banks.title: Use separate collection for a power bank
power-banks.text: Power banks contain a battery. Do not dismantle or put one in ordinary dry recycling. Ask the producer or a designated battery or e-waste collector for the local handover route.

sources.title: Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022

fluorescent-lamps.title: Keep fluorescent lamps for special-care collection
fluorescent-lamps.text: Keep the lamp intact and out of ordinary glass or dry recycling. Ask your local authority for a designated special-care or lamp collection point.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — special-care waste

led-bulbs.title: Keep LED bulbs out of ordinary glass recycling
led-bulbs.text: Ask your local authority or electrical retailer for a designated lamp or special-care collection route. Do not break the bulb to separate its materials.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — special-care waste

mobile-phone.title: Use an e-waste collection route
mobile-phone.text: Mobile phones are listed under India's E-Waste (Management) Rules. Back up and erase personal data, then ask the producer or a registered e-waste service how to hand over the phone.

sources.title: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 — Schedule I

laptop.title: Use an e-waste collection route
laptop.text: Laptops and computers are listed under India's E-Waste (Management) Rules. Back up and erase personal data, then check producer take-back or a registered e-waste service; do not dismantle the device yourself.

sources.title: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 — Schedule I

computer-mouse.title: Use an e-waste collection route for the mouse
computer-mouse.text: Keep the mouse out of ordinary dry recycling. Ask the producer or a registered e-waste service how to hand it over. If it has a removable battery, follow the product instructions and use the separate battery collection route.

sources.title: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 — scope and Schedule I

paper.title: Separate paper from wet waste
paper.text: Keep ordinary paper dry and separate for the dry-waste stream. Ask your local collector whether it accepts this particular paper product, especially if coated, used, or heavily soiled.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — dry waste

cardboard.title: Keep ordinary cardboard dry
cardboard.text: Separate clean, dry cardboard from wet waste and flatten it if your collector asks. Check local acceptance for coated or dirty cardboard.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — dry waste

glass.title: Keep ordinary glass separate from wet waste
glass.text: Ask your local collector whether it accepts this form of glass in its dry-waste or glass collection. Bottles, mirrors, cookware, and broken glass can have different routes.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — dry waste

metal.title: Separate ordinary metal items
metal.text: Keep ordinary metal items separate from wet waste. Ask your local collector or scrap service which sizes and forms it accepts; containers with chemical residue need another route.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — dry waste

plastic.title: Keep ordinary plastic waste separate from wet waste
plastic.text: India's Solid Waste Management Rules require waste to be separated at source. Keep ordinary plastic waste in the dry-waste stream and follow your local body's collection directions. Whether a specific plastic item can be recycled still depends on local acceptance and contamination.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — Rule 5

organic.title: Separate food scraps as wet waste
organic.text: Food waste is part of the wet-waste stream under India's Solid Waste Management Rules. Keep it separate from dry waste and follow your local body's collection or processing directions.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 — definitions and Rule 5
